source: Song, Gore, Kleiman-Weiner (2025/2026) Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents
finding: Empowerment of an LM agent, estimated from text trajectories (EELMA), tracks how well the agent performs, without a task reward.
numbers: Gridworld and Tower of Hanoi: estimates match direct channel-capacity values. Natural-language paraphrase: state RMSE 0.302 (Gridworld) and 0.438 (Hanoi) for direct estimation vs 0.048 and 0.127 for EELMA.
limits: Needs many trajectories (estimates stabilise near 50% of the data). Only a correlate of performance, not a controller.
agent_relevance: Empowerment is measurable on text agents. It could score which probe keeps the most future options open, but it is an evaluation signal, not a proven selector.

source: Song, Gore, Kleiman-Weiner (2025/2026) Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents (ablations)
finding: Removing chain-of-thought collapses empowerment, and empowerment follows performance across agent variants.
numbers: Disabling CoT: Gridworld 0.19 to 0.01 bits (99% drop); Hanoi 0.29 to 0.09 bits (65% drop). 1600 Gridworld and 800 Hanoi trajectories.
limits: Small toy games; model families differ across panels.
agent_relevance: Reasoning steps raise the agent's reach over future states; supports keeping a reasoning step before probe choice.

source: Song, Gore, Kleiman-Weiner (2025/2026) Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents (WebArena, tau-bench)
finding: Empowerment correlates with success in realistic web tasks, but the link breaks in some domains and when the agent wanders off task.
numbers: WebArena (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o3, Qwen2.5-32B): Spearman 0.83-0.94 in GitLab, Reddit, Shopping Admin; flat in Shopping. Qwen 'jailbreak': 40% (43/106) of trajectories left the sandbox, inflating empowerment while failing.
limits: Pooled Spearman only 0.39 on 16 model-domain pairs (WebArena) and 0.71 on 6 points (tau-bench). Reasoning-bound tasks (prices) are not limited by empowerment.
agent_relevance: Failed-replication flavour: raw diversity of states is not control. Any probe score must be checked against a task-relevant outcome.

source: Song, Gore, Kleiman-Weiner (2025/2026) Estimating the Empowerment of Language Model Agents (baselines)
finding: Simple trajectory statistics do worse than empowerment, but not by much in WebArena.
numbers: Spearman vs discounted reward, WebArena/tau-bench: empowerment 0.39/0.71; visitation entropy 0.16/-0.71; action entropy 0.09/-0.54; state coverage -0.04/-0.20; trajectory length -0.12/-0.54.
limits: Authors note the tau-bench value pools a success case with a floor-performance case; descriptive only.
agent_relevance: Plain coverage or diversity counts are misleading: diverse invalid actions look exploratory. Count only probes that change a checked outcome.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts: Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking in LLMs
finding: Choosing questions by simulated information gain (tree search over answers) raises task success over direct prompting.
numbers: Average +38.1% success rate over direct prompting across 5 datasets and 5 LLMs (+46.6% for Llama3-70B); beats CoT-SC by 33.8%, Reflexion by 29.9%, Original-ToT by 28.3%, Adapted-ToT by 12.4%. GPT-4 troubleshooting 43.7% to 67.3%; DX diagnosis 97.0%.
limits: Relative percentage gains as the paper reports them; answerer is GPT-4 (checked on 10% of games); simulation depth limited to 3 steps for cost.
agent_relevance: Direct support for choosing the S7 probe by expected uncertainty reduction, with a small tree, not by the model's feel for a good question.

source: Hu et al. (2024) UoT (comparators)
finding: Generic reasoning wrappers did not help question asking: CoT and PP were worse than GPT-4 alone in 20 Questions.
numbers: 20 Questions closed set: CoT (CS) and PP (CS) below plain GPT-4; UoT (OS) +8.7% over Adapted-ToT; UoT (CS) +4.3% over Reflexion.
limits: Same paper as b05; baselines implemented by the authors.
agent_relevance: Thinking harder in words is not the same as picking by information. Matches the rule that code, not the model, selects.

source: Choudhury et al. (2026) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design
finding: Explicit expected-information-gain choice by code roughly doubles 20 Questions success over prompting.
numbers: Average +37.4 percentage points over direct prompting across 6 LLMs and 3 problem sets (100 targets each); more than doubled in over half of setups and never decreased. Animals GPT-4o-mini: Prompt-Only 44, Split 78, BED-LLM 88. Celebrities Mistral-Large: 19, 63, 91. Llama-3.1-8B Animals: 8 to 63.
limits: Success is at 20 questions on an open entity space; standard errors 2-5 points per cell.
agent_relevance: Best current evidence that probe choice by EIG computed in code beats model judgment. Uses sampled hypotheses plus filtering, which we can copy.

source: Choudhury et al. (2026) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design (ablations)
finding: Each part matters: raw in-context beliefs, judgment instead of EIG, and entropy-only each lose a lot.
numbers: Animals GPT-4o: BED-LLM 93, Entropy 88, Data-estimation 70, ICL Beliefs 25, Implicit Maximisation 70, CoT 62, Prompt-Only 45. Celebrities Mistral-Large: BED 91, Entropy 68, ICL Beliefs 31, Implicit Max. 36.
limits: Ablation grid is one setting; the authors note their Split baseline is far stronger than in earlier papers.
agent_relevance: Filtering beliefs for consistency with past answers is the key repair (ICL beliefs 25 vs 93). Check a probe's hypotheses against the evidence in code.

source: Choudhury et al. (2026) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design (preference elicitation)
finding: The advantage shrinks when the target is a soft user profile rather than a concrete entity.
numbers: Film recommendation with 200 profiles: Prompt-Only is a stronger baseline than in 20 Questions; BED-LLM still gives higher-rated films, most clearly when questioner and answerer are different model classes.
limits: Small boost; the answerer scoring on a 1-5 scale is itself an LLM judgment.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: gains are largest where answers are crisp. For fuzzy probes expect smaller gains.

source: Mazzaccara, Testoni, Bernardi (2024) Learning to Ask Informative Questions: Preference Optimization and Expected Information Gain
finding: Training a 7B model with DPO on EIG-labelled question pairs raises question quality and success; plain fine-tuning on optimal questions can hurt success.
numbers: Llama-2-chat 7B, zero-shot vs FT vs DPO. INLG: S@1 56.7% / 46.6% / 68.9%; EIG 0.34 / 0.41 / 0.45. Things: 51.1% / 42.2% / 61.1%; EIG 0.29 / 0.31 / 0.40. Celebrities: 71.1% / 46.7% / 72.2%. Training data: 55,000 optimal (EIG=1) vs suboptimal (EIG<0.8) pairs.
limits: Higher EIG alone does not give success: FT raised EIG yet lowered S@1 in all three sets. Small 8-item candidate sets.
agent_relevance: EIG is a useful label but not the whole objective; an agent that maximises per-question EIG can still lose the game. Keep the final check separate.

source: Hartmann et al. (2026) Amortising Bayesian Experimental Design for Sequential Information Gathering in LLMs (ASIG)
finding: Reinforcement learning with an EIG reward teaches a 7B model to ask better questions, cheaply, but transfer is weak.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B: success more than doubles on 20 Questions and passes BED-LLM on animals; 14B gains only +4.2 (animals) and +1.8 (plants) points; 25x-36x cheaper than BED-LLM. MediQ (unseen): 7B accuracy 46.7 to 47.6, voluntary accuracy 50.1 to 51.8, overconfidence 36.1 to 33.4; 14B accuracy 54.1 to 54.2, voluntary accuracy 64.6 to 63.0, overconfidence 20.7 to 22.2.
limits: Workshop paper, 5 episodes; out-of-domain gain under 1 point on accuracy for 7B; 14B mixed.
agent_relevance: Training is not our route. Shows learned EIG skill transfers poorly, so a scaffold-side computation is the safer choice.

source: Dutta, Ramachandran, Sra (2026) Active Inference as Context Acquisition for AI Agents
finding: Frontier LLMs reduce uncertainty each turn but ask more questions than an exact optimal planner on clean 25-300 item guessing tasks.
numbers: 7 frontier models (GPT-5, GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Grok 4); binary 25 and 100 items; multiway 100, 200, 300 items; metric is mean extra questions vs a dynamic-programming oracle.
limits: Deterministic table lookup; exact numbers sit in figures; the active-inference step reduces to information gain per token cost.
agent_relevance: Even strong models leave questions on the table. A code-run greedy or short-lookahead selector over a candidate set should beat free asking. The paper itself notes greedy information gain is not always optimal.

source: Grand, Pepe, Tenenbaum, Andreas (2026) Shoot First, Ask Questions Later? Building Rational Agents that Explore and Act Like People
finding: On Collaborative Battleship, Monte Carlo EIG strategies lift weak LMs above humans and frontier models.
numbers: Humans N=42. Llama-4-Scout F1 0.367 to 0.764; GPT-4o 0.450 to 0.782; GPT-5 0.716 alone. Win rate vs humans 0.82-0.83; vs GPT-5 0.67 at 1% of GPT-5 cost (Scout) or 35% (GPT-4o). Spotter accuracy +14.7 points (Claude 4 Opus 86.8 to 94.4; GPT-4.1 75.2 to 90.9). Zero-EIG questions: Scout 18.5%, GPT-4o 14.6%. Guess Who: +28.3 to +42.4 points.
limits: GPT-5 gained little from Bayesian question or move selection, so strong reasoners may already approximate it. Spotter gain used code generation, not EIG alone.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence that a program-side EIG selector can substitute for model strength. Also a boundary: frontier reasoning models may not need it.

source: Grand et al. (2026) Shoot First (human comparison)
finding: Many LMs ask low-value questions that humans do not.
numbers: Llama-4-Scout 62.2% SpotterQA accuracy and 68.8% CaptainQA win rate vs random firing, marginally above random; human spotters 92.5%; on complex questions LMs fall from 72.8% to 60.4% accuracy.
limits: Single game type; humans N=42.
agent_relevance: Without a scaffold, models are weak at the exact thing S7 needs: choosing a probe that splits the hypotheses.

source: Zhang, Lu, Jaitly (2024) Probing the Multi-turn Planning Capabilities of LLMs via 20 Question Games
finding: Unaided LLMs find 20-Questions entities only about a third of the time at best; RL on game play helps small models.
numbers: GPT-4 about 1/3 of entities correctly identified; judge error 3.07% (Things) and 2.95% (Celebrities); Vicuna 13B and Mistral 7B not far behind some closed models; RL from game play (V-RLGP 13B) matched GPT-3.5 on in-domain Things.
limits: Strict exact-match scoring; later work (b07) reports its own prompt-only baseline improves on this one.
agent_relevance: Baseline for how poor unscaffolded probing is. The gap to b07 (88-95% on animals) is the room a scaffold can win.

source: Kobalczyk et al. (2025) Active Task Disambiguation with LLMs
finding: Choosing clarifying questions by information gain over sampled solutions beats reasoning in question space; weighting by the model's own log-probabilities is worse.
numbers: 20 Questions on 15 animals, 5 run seeds, 25 eval seeds, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini: EIG-uniform best; EIG-logprobs significantly worse; gap to implicit strategies much smaller for GPT-4o-mini.
limits: Plots rather than tables; assumes error-free pseudo-answers; small animal set.
agent_relevance: Boundary: if hypotheses are weighted by the model's own probabilities, bias creeps in. Sample hypotheses and weight them uniformly, or check with code.

source: Piriyakulkij, Kuleshov, Ellis (2024) Active Preference Inference using Language Models and Probabilistic Reasoning
finding: Out of the box, instruction-tuned LLMs ask uninformative preference questions; a probabilistic model whose terms are prompted from the LLM picks better ones.
numbers: Abstract states fewer user interactions are needed; numeric results not extracted this session.
limits: Only the first page was read for numbers.
agent_relevance: Earlier evidence for the same pattern as b07 and b16.

source: Yiu, Allen, Ginosar, Gopnik (2025) Empowerment Gain and Causal Model Construction (Star Machines study 1)
finding: Children and adults prefer machines that are both controllable and variable when they must produce new outcomes.
numbers: Study 1: 80 children (5-10 y, mean 7.52) and 120 adults (mean 27.57). Extra-small star: 46.25% children and 80.83% adults chose the right slot (chance 33%; p=.017 and p<.001). Hats: 56.26% children, 86.85% adults. Bright bulb: 71.74% / 76.67%; dim bulb 48.10% / 68.91%. Pure variability chosen 20% (children) and 5.04% (adults) for the extra-small star.
limits: Child accuracy often only just above chance; children favour pure variability more than adults, which the authors read as noise or information-gain interest. Behavioural, not a fit of an empowerment model.
agent_relevance: Human evidence that people choose interventions they can control and that map inputs to outcomes, not random variety. Supports preferring probes with predictable effect.

source: Massari, Biehl, Meeden, Kanai (2021) Experimental Evidence that Empowerment May Drive Exploration in Sparse-Reward Environments
finding: An empowerment-style bonus helps exploration only weakly; a curiosity (information-gain) agent was clearly better after removing an outlier run.
numbers: Four sparse-reward gridworlds, A2C baseline, 10 runs each. Time-to-success: no significant difference among the three agents with all runs kept. After removing the failed third run, the curious agent was significantly faster than baseline and the empowerment agent (e.g. t=2.29, p=0.024); empowerment vs baseline not significant in the cases read (p about 0.46 and 0.27).
limits: Small gridworlds, 10 runs, outlier removal after the fact, one-sided t-tests; authors say more work is needed to show empowerment consistently drives exploration.
agent_relevance: Counter-evidence: empowerment alone is not a reliable exploration drive. Information gain about the hypothesis is the better probe criterion.

source: Kumar (2018) Empowerment-driven Exploration using Mutual Information Estimation
finding: A DQN with a mutual-information empowerment bonus reaches the first-room rewards and enters the second room in Montezuma's Revenge.
numbers: Single game, qualitative learning curve; DQN baseline does not; no multi-seed table.
limits: Student report, one game, no statistics.
agent_relevance: Weak positive evidence; do not rely on it.

source: Levy, Allievi, Konidaris (2024) Latent-Predictive Empowerment
finding: Empowerment can be computed without a simulator by a latent-predictive model.
numbers: Matches skillset size of the leading model-based empowerment method in high-dimensional and stochastic settings and beats other model-based methods (abstract-level claim; ICLR 2025 submission).
limits: Under-review draft; per-environment tables not extracted.
agent_relevance: Shows empowerment estimation is still a research problem; do not build it into the scaffold.

source: Garg, Myers, Li, Ji, Eysenbach, Levine (2026) Measuring Empowerment from Offline Data for Intrinsically Motivated Exploration
finding: First estimator of empowerment from offline data; the bonus helps on some tasks and does not hurt, but is fragile.
numbers: OGBench, 5 seeds. Adding the bonus beat CRL on cube-single-play, cube-single-noisy, antmaze-medium-navigate, antmaze-medium-stitch, pointmaze-teleport-stitch; on par elsewhere. Four prior empowerment estimators failed to recover a usable map (DADS saturates at log K; DV-empowerment unbounded). Behaviour-cloning coefficient: empowerment collapses at 1e-2 on antsoccer-stitch; usable range about one order of magnitude.
limits: Needs a tuned regulariser; low-coverage data breaks it.
agent_relevance: Gains are task-specific and sensitive to one hyper-parameter, so empowerment is not a robust general-purpose probe criterion.

source: Schneider et al. (2025) Information-Theoretic Policy Pre-Training with Empowerment
finding: Empowerment-pretrained policies learn faster downstream in gridworlds, with mixed results on strong actor-critic methods.
numbers: Gridworld: empowerment-based agents consistently beat from-scratch agents, most for REINFORCE; with PPO no clear improvement but no degradation.
limits: Small domains; authors attribute limited gains to strong baselines.
agent_relevance: Value is early data efficiency, which does not transfer to a prompting agent.

source: Kobayashi (2026) Flexible Empowerment at Reasoning with Extended Best-of-N Sampling
finding: Using empowerment inside best-of-N action choice gives small, task-dependent gains.
numbers: Interquartile mean return (8 seeds), Random / H-BoN / S-BoN / E-BoN: Cheetah 264.47 / 263.61 / 264.84 / 280.97; Walker 300.59 / 313.68 / 290.28 / 301.38; Quadruped 438.57 / 395.56 / 398.13 / 416.37.
limits: E-BoN best only on Cheetah; random sampling best on Quadruped; H-BoN best on Walker.
agent_relevance: No robust win for empowerment-weighted selection. Do not expect empowerment to beat information gain at probe choice.

source: Burda et al. (2018) Large-Scale Study of Curiosity-Driven Learning
finding: Prediction-error curiosity works without any task reward across 54 environments, but is broken by self-generated noise.
numbers: 54 environments (48 Atari). Inverse-dynamics features beat random features in 55% of Atari games; pixel-based curiosity works poorly; random features are a strong baseline. In a 3D task the agent rewards itself without progress when it controls a noisy source (noisy TV).
limits: Prediction error is not information gain; it rewards unlearnable noise.
agent_relevance: Noisy-TV warning: a probe whose result is random looks informative to a surprise measure. Information gain over a checked hypothesis set does not share this fault.

source: Millidge, Tschantz, Buckley (2020) Whence the Expected Free Energy?
finding: The exploratory term of active inference does not follow from free-energy minimisation; a natural extension of free energy actively discourages exploration.
numbers: Theoretical: expected free energy is not simply the free energy in the future. Proposes a Free-Energy of the Expected Future that keeps the epistemic term plus a divergence between predicted and desired futures.
limits: Mathematical argument, no behavioural test.
agent_relevance: Rival-theory point: active inference's exploration is built in, not derived. For us it reduces to expected information gain plus a preference term.

source: Kulveit, von Stengel, Leventov (2023) Predictive Minds: LLMs as Atypical Active Inference Agents
finding: Conceptual claim that LLMs fit active inference except for a missing action-perception loop.
numbers: No experiments.
limits: Position paper.
agent_relevance: Not evidence for any scaffold gain.

source: Klyubin, Polani, Nehaniv (2005) Empowerment: a universal agent-centric measure of control
finding: Founding definition: empowerment is the channel capacity between an agent's actions and its later sensor states.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Cited from memory and via b01, b19.
agent_relevance: Defines the quantity b01 estimates for LMs.

source: Friston et al. (2015, 2017) Active inference and epistemic value
finding: Founding work on expected free energy with an epistemic term.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Cited from memory; theory critique is b26.
agent_relevance: Background only.

source: Ruggeri and Lombrozo (2015) Children adapt their questions to achieve efficient search
finding: Children move toward more informative questions with age in 20 Questions.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Cited from memory; no numbers recorded.
agent_relevance: Human baseline for b14 and b15, but unverified.
